title: Answering Job Interview Questions
speaker: Oxford Online English
description: Gina demonstrates concise interview answers, signposting, the STAR structure and reflecting the interviewer’s key words.
summary: The lesson works through common interview questions and ways to keep answers structured. It explains signposting, situation/task/action/result examples and reflecting useful words from a question.

title: Writing Emails in English
speaker: Oxford Online English
description: Mike explains how to organise an email, state its purpose, add details and write a clear request or call to action.
summary: The lesson builds an email through opening, purpose, supporting details, requests and closing. It considers how the writer’s relationship with the reader affects wording and politeness.

title: Formal Email Phrases
speaker: Oxford Online English
description: The lesson models formal email openings, introducing a purpose, arranging appointments and closing politely.
summary: The lesson models formal email openings, introducing a purpose, arranging appointments and closing politely.

title: English for Team Projects

title: How to Prepare for an Interview
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: BBC Learning English's English at Work episode on preparing for a job interview with confidence and concrete examples.
summary:
This BBC Learning English episode from the English at Work series follows Anna as she prepares for a job interview. It gives learners a concrete workplace scenario rather than abstract advice, making it useful for role-play and speaking practice.

The source focuses on preparation before the interview: researching the role, sounding confident without becoming arrogant, and preparing examples that show useful workplace qualities. It gives students language for presenting strengths, talking about achievements, and explaining why they are suitable for a position.

For ESL classes, the video works well as the first lesson in an interview course because it sets up the situation and introduces the emotional pressure of interviews. Students can identify useful interview adjectives, practise short self-introductions, and build evidence-based answers instead of giving one-word claims.

title: Answering Interview Questions
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: BBC Learning English's English at Work episode on answering interview questions clearly when you cannot find the exact word.
summary:
This BBC Learning English episode continues Anna's interview and focuses on answering questions under pressure. The scene is useful because learners hear an imperfect answer develop into a clearer one, which makes the language problem realistic and teachable.

The source gives students practice with motivation language, paraphrasing, and repairing answers when they cannot remember a precise word. It also supports discussion of what makes an interview answer persuasive: clarity, enthusiasm, evidence, and relevance to the role.

For a course lesson, teachers can use it to move from preparation into live answer practice. Students can rewrite weak answers, build alternative phrases, and role-play follow-up questions from the interviewer.

title: Responding to Competency Questions
speaker: British Council | English
description: British Council English video on responding to competency-based job interview questions.
summary:
This British Council English video focuses on competency-based job interview questions: prompts where candidates need to show evidence from their past experience. It is short enough to use as a model before students build and practise their own answers.

The source is useful for teaching answer structure. Students can notice how a strong response names the situation, explains the action taken, and connects the result to the job. It pairs naturally with STAR-method practice, peer feedback, and mock interview rounds.

For ESL learners, the value is practical and immediate: they practise past-tense storytelling, workplace verbs, achievement language, and concise explanation under interview pressure.

title: Talking About Your Job
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: Mike models ways to describe your job, employer, responsibilities and how you feel about your work.
summary: The lesson practises employment status, job roles and everyday responsibilities. It offers adjectives such as rewarding and challenging and invites learners to describe their own work.

title: Making Small Talk in English
speaker: Oxford Online English
description: Oli models small-talk questions and answers, ways to extend a conversation and topics that may be too personal.
summary: The lesson shows how everyday small talk helps people connect. It models topics such as home towns and discusses how context and culture affect personal questions.

title: Work and Business Discussions
speaker: BBC Learning English
description: A compilation of BBC discussions about returning to the office, self-employment, workplaces without bosses and product lifecycles.
summary: A compilation of BBC discussions about returning to the office, self-employment, workplaces without bosses and product lifecycles.
